Sharing an airplane can mean more chances to fly—and more people to fly with. ✈️💙

Lake Missoula Flight Club in Montana has been recognized as the 300th club formed through the AOPA Foundation’s Flying Clubs Initiative.

AOPA’s October 14 announcement describes a club with 30 members, ages 22 to 75, and five airplanes: two Cessna 150s, a Grumman AA-1C Lynx, a Piper Tri-Pacer and a Cessna 182.

The idea is practical. Hangar space, insurance and annual maintenance create costs even when an airplane isn’t flying. A club spreads those expenses among members while giving them access to aircraft.

But the payoff goes beyond the budget. Members describe a place to find flying companions, regain currency and keep building skills after initial training.

The initiative began in 2015 and has helped establish clubs in 45 states. The 300th-club milestone was celebrated October 8.

More shared airplanes. More flying friendships. More reasons to keep that certificate working.

Source: AOPA, October 14, 2026
